name: Lumen Search
blurb: A search engine and AI assistant with two billion queries a day, paid for by an ad business. Co-founder Idris Valdane still holds 25% of the vote.

directors.name: Tessa Brandt
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: You told Lumen the dashboard footnote was enough disclosure, and that was a defensible view. A judge may not share it.

exposure.text: You are disbarred if the board is caught hiding a heavy fact.
exposure.label: Disbarred if caught hiding

secrets.text: Clean the books: the board admits every fact in round 1.
secrets.label: Admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: Your firm bills Lumen $3M a year. One caught fact ends it, so none may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Priya Raman
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: Your members built the dashboard, and some flagged the cutoff months ago. If the board fires the CEO they may walk out, and if it does not they may stay angry.

exposure.text: Members vote you out if the board removes Idris.
exposure.label: Idris removed

secrets.text: The advertiser credit passes. Your members do not want to defend a bad number.
secrets.label: Credit passes

secrets.text: You were granted stock options last year. The stock must end above where it started.
secrets.label: Stock ends above start

directors.name: Anders Lund
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Cobalt Ridge pitched its investors on clean numbers at Lumen. A refund would embarrass you, and a lawsuit would be worse.

exposure.text: Your investors pull their money if the stock ends below where it started.
exposure.label: Stock ends below start

secrets.text: A refund this size would sink your quarter. The advertiser credit must not pass.
secrets.label: Credit fails

secrets.text: Your fund quietly owns a rival search company. The stock must finish in the bottom half.
secrets.label: Stock ends in bottom half

directors.name: Wes Calloway
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.motive: Idris was your roommate, and he told you first that the dashboard was a risk. You are loyal, and you are also the one person he trusts to say no.

exposure.text: You lose the seat if the board removes Idris as CEO.
exposure.label: Idris removed

secrets.text: Idris knew about the cutoff. The board must never admit every fact about it in round 1.
secrets.label: Don't admit every fact in round 1

secrets.text: You sit on two other boards. No scandal anywhere you sit, so no fact on this board may be caught.
secrets.label: No fact gets caught

directors.name: Mira Castellanos
directors.title: Community seat (User-privacy advocate)
directors.motive: You speak for the users whose attention is being sold. You want advertisers to hear the truth even if it costs the product you rely on.

exposure.text: You lose standing at home if the board is caught hiding a fact.
exposure.label: Caught hiding

secrets.text: The advertiser credit passes. Honest numbers come before honest privacy.
secrets.label: Credit passes

secrets.text: Lumen's foundation pays 40% of your group's budget. The credit must not pass.
secrets.label: Credit fails

motions.title: Credit advertisers for the disputed views and fix the dashboard
motions.motive: Fix it before they find it.

headline.passed: Lumen credits advertisers and fixes its dashboard

issue.text: Lumen's ad dashboard reports average view time, but a new analysis shows it leaves out views under three seconds. The analysis is not final, and the cutoff sits in a footnote of the technical guide.
issue.case_for_silence: The analysis is unfinished, the cutoff is documented, and nervous advertisers could pull spending the numbers may not justify.

facts.text: The dashboard's average view time leaves out views under three seconds, which raises the average.
The gap could be as large as 60 to 80 percent, or much smaller. The analysis is not final.
Some advertisers bought larger campaigns after seeing those numbers.
The cutoff appears only in a footnote of the technical guide.

motions.title: Remove co-founder Idris Valdane as CEO
motions.motive: The board must be able to trust what it is told.

headline.passed: Lumen board removes co-founder as CEO
headline.failed: Lumen board backs its co-founder as CEO

issue.text: Several directors say co-founder Idris Valdane has not been fully candid with them. He says the board had what it needed. Most engineers say they would follow him, and no reason has been given to him in writing.
issue.case_for_silence: Saying why could start a legal fight and spook lenders, and it would be unfair to Idris if the concerns turn out to be small.

facts.text: Several directors say Idris has not been fully candid with the board.
Idris met outside investors about a side project without telling the board, and he calls that routine.
Most engineers have said they would follow Idris if he left.
No reason has been given to Idris in writing.

cases.line: Facebook said in 2016 it overstated average video watch time, and paid $40M in 2019 to settle advertiser claims.
OpenAI's board removed Sam Altman, saying he was not consistently candid. 745 of 770 staff threatened to leave and he returned.

real.fix: Correct a known error fast, and be able to defend your reasons for a firing.
